So my standards of coverage are not to hype the good news without talking about the difficulties and complex macro and social realities. The AI market needs to face its reality too and fundamentals. I will try to curate a bunch of data points to help you get a more holistic picture of the reality of BigTech, BigAI and financing risks, as well as the experience of consumers and the market.

Share

Nvidia, Reflection AI and Meta just released New Open-Source Models

Reflection’s Beam scores second among US open weights models: Beam scores 30, behind only Meta's Muse Spark Open (39) and ahead of yesterday’s NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (26) release. The numbers represent scores on AA. It’s less clear if this will protect from token marketshare gains for Chinese open-weight models:

Does Beam, Muse Spark Open and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Protect?

WHAT DO YOU THINK? (Vote)

Reflection’s Beam is a nice addition.

Muse partnered with Apple and claims that Muse Spark Open is optimized to run on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.

The AI Financing Breakdown of Autumn, 2026

The gap between what it costs to build AI infrastructure and what companies are actually paying to use it is widening, even as, a massive gap is opening up between AI infrastructure spending and expected returns. The accelerating demand for compute is leading to sharper negative FCF Earnings by BigTech. According to Gartner and others, more than $4 trillion in AI infrastructure spending could be at risk of write-downs by the end of 2032 if companies maintain their current investment pace.

Neo Cloud volatility and coverage centered around Oracle, CoreWeave and Softbank are starting to get more attention. As we had mentioned earlier, Gartner predicts that more than 80% of specialized so-called Neo Clouds will likely cease operating independently by 2030. There’s an infographic for that! But not somehow the full realization yet in the market. By the end of 2026 and heading into 2027, it will get much harder to secure financing. That is, Global AI-related debt issuance plunged to $23 billion in September 2026, down sharply from $113 billion in June, per the Financial Times. A major financing crunch for AI could be right around the corner.

The Demand for Compute and Mismatch is going to get more Extreme

While AI sentiment continues to worsen with datacenter moratoriums, Banks are also actively pulling back to avoid concentration risk in 2026, with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon confirming his bank is tightening up on credit. Approximately $18 billion in bank loans for an Oracle data center campus recently slid into stressed territory, while Nvidia-backed AI cloud provider Firmus shelved an IPO that sought a valuation north of $30 billion. Nscale luckily has Anthropic contract rumors. Anthropic and Nscale IPOs will be ones to watch.

In a nutshell, there is a massive gap between AI spending and AI revenue, one that won't close for many, many years (if it ever does).

In a world where Anthropic is a Neo Cloud customer of SpaceX. Plainly? Anthropic is currently one of the “largest anchor customers” for SpaceX’s newly expanded "Neocloud" AI compute division, utilizing the full capacity of SpaceX’s Colossus 1 data center in Memphis.

Anthropic’s Balance Sheet Worse than we Thought

Anthropic brought in just $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026 (surpassing its full-year 2025 revenue of $4.6 billion). However, the company reported a massive net loss of $80.7 billion for the first half of 2026. But don’t worry, that’s other people’s money.

The general release of their S-1 to the public is soon, likely next week or 15 days before their IPO. The company logged a $42 billion net loss in 2025, which basically doubled.

SpaceX Squeezes Cursor made Grok Bot Growth and Neo Cloud Revenue

By the Numbers:

  • SpaceX reported Q3 2026 revenue of $14.58 billion and net income of $4.4 billion.

  • Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Infrastructure Segment makes up 52% of the revenue for SpaceX, which is officially no longer a rocket launch company, but something else entirely. A Neo Cloud with decent Grok Bot growth. The Cursor acquisition is paying off already.

  • Consumer Starlink subscribers grew by 1.6 million during the quarter to reach 13.6 million total users growing at a 69% YOY clip. Still one of the main drivers of the overall business.

However in Q3 SpaceX is also spending big on Capex with a lot of debt. Q3 2026 Capex: $19.6 billion (a significant step up from $6.9 billion in Q3 2025 and $18.37 billion in Q2 2026). They have $38.8 billion in debt, with 78% inside ownership (mostly Elon Musk).

  • SpaceX’s launch business generated just $1.77 billion in revenue in the third quarter. They are now nearly totally dependent on the AI and Starlink narrative story.

SpaceX will do Capex as if its a Hyperscaler

  • Elon Musk guided to $35B to $40B of capex for the fourth quarter (Q4) of 2026, putting it in line with Microsoft's capex spend in the most recent quarter.

  • The dream of orbital compute and Terafab aren’t going to come cheap.

AI is Inflationary Pushing the Affordability crisis to new highs in the U.S.

articles.content:
Good Morning,
Today we move ahead in our 🗺️AI guides series. You can always check out more of our applied AI guides here.
By the way, if you run an AI Newsletter on Substack and write AI guides and want to be featured in a guest post that can drive some more traffic than usual, you can DM me on LinkedIn here.
Since the launch of Meta’s Muse, there’s been a significant uptick in so-called personal agents. ChatGPT has so many users, so it will be interesting to see what they can do with dots. Using AI to run asynchronously in its own cloud environment is simply the new normal in 2026 both for work and personal tasks.
ChatGPT in recent months have added so many more options with Codex, ChatGPT Work and other new additions. OpenAI claims Dots are always-on AI agents integrated into the ChatGPT ecosystem. I asked to give us a simple but detailed guide to OpenAI’s AI agents called Dots.
📚 I’m running a limited time discount in case you want to support my work and financially anchor my ability to continue doing this, you can upgrade here. I am grateful for the support.
The two themes on AI Supremacy in October, 2026 are (State of AI type) AI Infographics and AI applied how-to guides. In case these approaches interest you.
A great publication for building with AI, not just to learn how to prompt.
is trending on the technology rising leaderboard of Substack due to his helpful AI guides. Gencay Işık is a former mechanical engineer and AI consultant. As you may know I’m a huge fan of supporting international and foreign writers in the space and his guides are very detailed and easy to follow.
is an AI educator, engineer, and content creator who specializes in teaching people how to build and monetize practical AI systems, agents, and automation workflows. He is a former mechanical engineer and data scientist who transitioned full-time into the AI space. His ability to reverse-engineer AI products and find innovative ways to monetize AI is really fun too - Here are a few that stood out to me:
Claude Code for Beginners: The Complete Course in One Post
I Built 10 NotebookLMs From MIT, Hormozi and Buffett
I Gave OpenAI Dots $600 to Trade
I Built a Claude Skill That Makes $700K/Year
OpenAI introduced dots on their lats OpenAI DevDay about two weeks ago. This is the guide by of the Newsletter LearnAIWithMe.
“Unlike Codex or ChatGPT, Dots are meant to operate independent of any specific hardware or interface, pursuing user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight.”
OpenAI released Dots on September 29, and I’ve been testing it ever since.
OpenAI introduced Dots on September 29, powered by GPT-6 Astra.
Now let’s jump straight in.
To reach Dots, you need a ChatGPT Pro plan.
Pro comes in three usage tiers: $100, $200, and $500.
All three include Dots. I’m on the first one.
The rollout is gradual, so it can take a few days to show up in your account. If you can’t find it, open chatgpt.com/dots.
After you upgrade your account, click on “Your dot” and then “Continue”.
Step 1. Open Your dot and click Continue.
Next, it asks you to connect your apps to make it more helpful.
Step 2. Dots asks to connect your apps. You can skip it.
Since I don’t have any annoying meetings on my calendar, I clicked on “Continue without connecting additional plugins.”
Next, it started setting up my Dot and asked me to wait a couple of minutes.
Step 3. Setting up your Dot takes a couple of minutes.
I feel like I bought a new Apple product and am setting it up. At this step, it asked me to choose where my Dot can work.
It even has its own cloud computer, so it can keep working while I’m away from my laptop.
But I also wanted it to read my files, so I selected it like this below.
Step 4. Choose where your Dot can work and what it can read.
It wants me to customize it, and it answers me in both Turkish and English because I talk to it in two languages.
Your Dot answers in the languages you already use with it.
I clicked on “Customize your dot”.
Step 5. Click Customize your dot.
I named my Dot after my favorite TV show character, with a little adjustment.
(Burhan Altintop + Alfred the butler = Alfred Altintop)
And I picked the following “characters” and “pets”, and clicked on “Save”.
Pick a character and a pet, then save. Mine is Alfred Altintop.
When I clicked his name:
Click your Dot’s name to open its page.
This page opens.
Here I can call him, connect with him via Slack, and see his tasks.
Your Dot’s page. Call it, connect on Slack, see its tasks.
Being able to call it is a really powerful feature.
Dots are very similar to OpenClaw, Hermes, or Grok bots, but being able to call your Dot is a huge differentiator.
Here is the conversation.
Your Dot doesn’t live only inside ChatGPT. You can connect it to Slack.
To do that, I clicked the Slack icon here:
Step 1. Click the Slack button on your Dot’s profile.
Next, it asks for my approval. I clicked on “Add to Slack”.
Step 2. Pick your workspace and click Add to Slack.
After a few seconds, it connects. Then click Open Slack.
Step 3. Connected. Click Open Slack.
And here it is, ready on Slack.
Alfred’s first message on Slack.
You can now talk to it on Slack. Add it to a channel, mention it, and it answers in the thread, like this.
Mention your Dot in a channel, and it replies in the thread.
You can check your Slack connection from here.
Alfred’s profile. Slack sits right next to Call.
It’s the same Dot with the same memory. Moving from ChatGPT to Slack doesn’t reset anything.
One gotcha. Adding your Dot to a channel doesn’t mean it watches that channel. To make it monitor, tell it which channels to check, what to watch for, and when to ping you. Then ask it to confirm the recurring task.
My favorite idea from OpenAI’s own docs.
Keep routine progress in ChatGPT, and send only the decisions to Slack.
(If your Slack belongs to a company workspace, your admin has to turn Dots on first.)
Read more

articles.title: Is Meta Muse Too Good to be True?
articles.content:
Good Morning,
I’m running a limited time discount in case you want to support my work and financially anchor my ability to continue doing this, you can upgrade here.
Grateful to have the support.
Nathan Benaich and Air Street Capital released the 9th edition of their incredible State of AI 2026 report. I’ve been covering this every year since I started AI Supremacy because it’s a great snapshot and reminder of where we are at with some unique takes.
Many of the charts today will come from this source. It’s easier to read these infographics on a computer.
Check out our first batch of explorations of the State of AI 2026 infographics here. Today we’ll go a bit further into the report.
This week Meta released its Muse Wonder model and claimed that Muse has 5 million downloads after just 22 days. While Muse Wonder is also a speedy model, the speed of who is blocking the Muse personal agent is equally fascinating. So far:
Multiple Telecom Carriers
eBay
Automated Cloudflare Blocks at scale (thousands of websites).
Anthropic shared a blog about its recent advances in anti-distillation protocols. About to go IPO in just weeks, Anthropic says early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%. This appears to have led to a slowing down of Chinese Open-weight Model releases in Autumn, 2026.
“Preventing distillation is important both for our national security and for ensuring that powerful models, especially publicly available ones, are released with adequate safeguards.”
This according to the accelerationist leaning Epoch.AI.
Google has finally given the world access to its latest frontier model, after a seven month delay since its last one. According to Google, Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Muse Wonder Full and Gemini 4 Argon land in a very similar scoring tier, roughly on par with OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, and roughly well behind Anthropic Opus 5.5.
Google says Argon is especially adept for Enterprise customers:
To solve major engineering problems like large codebase refactoring and optimizations
To optimize business workflows across domains like legal, finance, and science
To find and patch critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities
There’s a certain degree of uncertainty with regards to the impact of Generative AI on major industries and the macro economy as compute and models ramp up. I think for healthcare, education and biotechnology we’ll have to wait some more time to see.
Europe’s ability to keep up and even adopt and adapt at the level of the United States and China is in some doubt. Europe has neither the capital advantages of America or the talent and energy abundance of China.

articles.title: Borrowed Time: How Rising Rates Reach the AI Build-Out
articles.content:
Good Morning,
This month full disclosure I’m having a family health issue, so I have less time for research and writing than my usual.
I’m running a limited time discount in case you want to support my work and financially anchor my ability to continue doing this, you can upgrade here. Due to these personal circumstances, the publication may include more guest contributor posts in October than usual. Grateful to have the support.
Recently changes in the macro landscape have triggered renewed concerns over an AI bubble, monetization deficits, margin debt with dangerously rising yields compounded by circular vendor financing, circular financing among BigTech, and significant concentration worries that now nearly totally clouds the AI infra roll-out picture.
As I’m not a macro analyst, I asked (see LinkedIn), who is a Dubai-based macroeconomic analyst, financial writer, and investment strategist to take a look at the prospects of an AI bubble given all of this recent pressure.
I hope you are in the mood for reading and understanding about how the big picture could impact the AI boom, Capex and the AI bull market.
Global Macro & Financial Market insights. About section.
“MacroVisor takes a top-down view of markets, tracking the trend and cycle shifts that often show up in the macro data before they are fully priced. Our research is rigorous but accessible, written for investors who want to understand the story behind the numbers.”
I’m a huge fan of Ayesha’s Notes on the Substack app that help me keep up with the macro picture. More from the author:
US Q3, 2026 Earnings Preview: Record Profits Meet 5% Yields
Why a Diesel Export Ban Could Actually Raise Gasoline Prices
Meanwhile the head market strategist at Panmure Liberum projects that the AI bubble will likely burst in 2027 or 2028, noting that heavy capital is flowing into resource-intensive frontier models. His thesis around local AI and small language models prevailing is super interesting. He’s joins a growing chorus of bears on the AI bubble and was recently on Bloomberg to explain his thesis.
MacroVisor (not a sponsor) is an independent financial research and strategy firm that specializes in global macroeconomics, thematic investing, and cross-asset class strategies in the UAE. This is based on Ayesha Tariq’s expertise of over 20 years working in the field. With higher bond yields globally the accounting for AI Infrastructure begins to look a lot more risky.
Driven by persistent inflationary pressures and seemingly heavy government debt issuance, bonds are rising at an alarming rate in the second half of 2026.
If this post is useful to you or someone you know, kindly share it.
By (Early October, 2026).

Good Morning,
Editor’s note: This month full disclosure I’m having a family health issue, so I have less time for research and writing than my usual. Nathan Benaich and Air Street Capital released the 9th edition of their incredible State of AI 2026 report. I’ve been covering this every year since I started AI Supremacy because it’s a great snapshot and reminder of where we are at with some unique takes.
Many of the charts today will come from this source.
Five weeks from the Anthropic IPO, Anthropic released their latest iteration of Haiu 5.5. Claude Haiku 5.5 is of course their cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model where they claim it costs around 75% less to run than Claude Haiku 4.5. Haiku 5.5 is considered to be the world’s frontier model in its class.
Nathan in the State of AI report insinuates that Google and OpenAI share the “frontier lab” placement with Anthropic, but I do not believe this is the case. Anthropic going IPO for me is the sole frontier model builder now in the world weeks to months ahead of all other AI labs.
I can understand The State of AI’s thesis of three labs sharing the frontier though:
The State of AI report is backwards looking and is written weeks before the present.
Full disclosure Nathan Benaich is a British VC, so their report will have an AI accelerationist bias and may not report on social, public and civic issues that are important for the macro context. However for academic and industry synthesis, it’s a highly respected report:
Air Street Press have a Newsletter, have made decent picks in the development of Generative AI and AI startups in general. Nathan also has a 33 minutes video review of the State of AI 2026 report you can check out on his most recent article on Substack. I have no affiliation with them, some of their best bets include:
Benchmarks built to last years they say, are now saturating in months. It’s not entirely clear how to evaluate this.
“We urge mathematicians to discontinue their work with OpenAI and to return to a vision of science that centers human understanding.”
The backlash to AI is only just beginning.
Terry Tao via the Association for Human Mathematics Communications Working Group. Read the full statement.
Read the blog here. This is a response to OpenAI exaggerating its capabilities when on October 6th, 2026, OpenAI published a GitHub repository (
openai/math) containing 722 mathematical manuscripts (grouped into 372 subject families) tackling open research problems and long-standing mathematical conjectures.
AI’s role in the future of science is open for debate. OpenAI stated that out of roughly 4,000 posed problems, each generated paper consumed an average of about 3 hours of "ChatGPT Pro thinking compute".
A report by the Financial Times indicated that OpenAI’s annualized revenue as of late September 2026 stood at approximately $50 billion, which was roughly $20 billion lower than the $70 billion figure that had previously circulated in financial media. So we know that A significant portion of OpenAI's enterprise revenue comes through cloud distribution partners like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google.
According to FT reporting, the discrepancy arose from attempts by OpenAI's own investors to produce a direct comparison with Anthropic's annualized revenue. Annualized revenue run rate (ARR) is sometimes misleading sales metric, which often involves multiplying one month's revenue by 12. It’s not clear what led OpenAI to exaggerate its financial progress to profitability.
Nous Research may become a serious player in the personal agent B2C space for individual developers and AI first adopters. They have raised $90 Million in a Series B, but also have an Enterprise Hermes on the way. This is an incredible sign for the capability and future of open-source agents. The round was led by Robot Ventures, with participation from other backers including Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung, and 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner.
Nous Research’s will begin a more organized push into the enterprise sector with “Hermes for Businesses,” allowing companies to deploy customized AI agents that can handle multi-step workflows while keeping their data private and secure. Nous was formed in 2023. There’s been a sudden influx of funding for personal assistants since the popularity of Meta’s Muse. Including Underdog (via Conway Research), Hark and Tab.
These are estimates from Similarweb, when Meta only had 3 millions weekly users just a few days earlier according to The Information based off of internal Meta data. It’s hard to tell how well Muse app downloads are translating into MAUs, let along weekly or daily active users. The Muse product appears in 2026 far less sticky than Chatbots were in 2023.
Hard to believe that this is the 9th edition of State of AI by Nathan Benaich. View the full report.
OpenAI’s study of agent adoption finds the fastest growth among non-developers, including people in legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing. Obviously OpenAI has been pushing Codex as its 1.2 billion weekly users of ChatGPT have more options. Outside of individual plans, there are around 9 million corporate/business seats across ChatGPT Team, Enterprise, and Edu offerings. The adoption of Codex however is key to its ability for sustained Enterprise revenue.
AI is already helping build better AI. According to Anthropic’s internal index, Claude led 26% of measured model R&D work in August, up from under 1% in February. How fast will internal model RSI teams accelerate new more powerful models?
Researchers set the tasks and supervise execution, and Anthropic reports that this is speeding up development.
Skild’s S1 performed unfamiliar tasks from video demonstrations without updating its weights. With 100,000 hours of pre-training, it scored 66% on the company’s cumulative per-step success measure, against 9% for a language-prompted baseline trained on the same data and compute.
I have written about this trend already here.
If 2026 is around GPT-2 level, when do we arrive at GPT-3 or GPT-4 for robotics and humanoids with general purpose utility.
AI-assisted drug discovery is finally reaching late-stage clinical development. Generate:Biomedicines’ GB-0895 for severe asthma and Insilico’s rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis are recruiting in Phase 3. Enveda’s ENV-294 is in placebo-controlled Phase 2a trials for eczema and asthma. Human trials are of course the ultimate test and will determine whether these medicines are safe and effective.
Do this give AI in drug development a more viable path? Will Anthropic continue going further into biology, computational and synthetic biology and biotechnology? It appears they are interested in doing so. While projects like Biohub are expanding, even as China moves ahead in some aspects of biotech and new drugs.
As the demand for compute accelerates but the cost per token is declining rapidly, inference has become the significant intersection of revenue and commercial capture. Meanwhile the cost of Capex and datacenters has risen tremendously due to HBM costs and other supply bottlenecks. This creates a severe environmental press and bottleneck for how fast and meaningful compute has become while AI sentiment continues to degrade both from ordinary American consumers and in politics. As models become more capable with declining prices, Chinese open-weight models have gained market. This is probably the biggest single that has occured in 2026 in AI.
With Anthropic going IPO in five days, they have shown incredible ARR Growth. We will soon have more details about via their S-1 that will go public a few weeks before the date. As for the first period of 2026, OpenAI and Anthropic’s combined reported annualized revenue run rates reached an astonishing $105B by late summer, up from about $30B at the start of the year. That’s more than 3x.
Research firm New Constructs wrote in a note on Tuesday that Anthropic’s IPO would be “the most ridiculous IPO of 2026,” posing a historic risk to financial markets. With a $2 Trillion valuation, we will soon find out what the market thinks.
I don’t believe personally that Google or OpenAI can be characterized as frontier model builders any longer and that Chinese open-weight models should take more token marketshare in 2027. "The Big Short" investor Michael Burry highlighted the valuation gap between Anthropic and established S&P 500 companies, noting that Anthropic's valuation equals the combined value of 78 S&P 500 companies, including top household brands and established industrial firms. A lot is riding on the IPOs of Anthropic and OpenAI (presuming OpenAI does go public in the first half of 2027).
Anthropic’s premium high-spend token share should continue as the leading frontier and Enterprise AI company in 2027, but I don’t believe OpenAI can keep up. OpenAI had to hit pause on Astra 6.1 due to alignment and cybersecurity issues. That is totally unprecedented for a company losing as much money as OpenAI continues to do. This is not what super intelligence looks like! I never trust any post lumping these two companies together.
The success of Claude Cowork and its business plugins across legal, finance, marketing and more brought whiplashing uncertainty to software markets. Aided by some fairly deceptive macro (Citrini was later sold to Semianalysis along with its x following) coverage. Nearly $285B was wiped from software stocks in two weeks during February’s “SaaSpocalypse.” This thesis that AI will be disruptive to SaaS companies continues to persist, when while at the same time I will note that SaaS companies are some of the best at executing new high-growth products related to LLMs.
With a significant rise in State wide datacenter moratoriums, AI is becoming a political issue. More AI requires financing, construction, and local consent. But these are not infinite where in 2026 AI sentiment sourced considerably for most people. This as a European plan is seeking up to €10B in public funding and at least €20B privately. While IPOs like Nscale will test “Sovereign compute” in places like Norway. Most funding of European AI, robotics and datacenter initiatives actually comes from the U.S.
China also had a much higher cadence of new models in the first nine months of 2026. Where it took Google 7 months from February to late September to even release a flagship model (that is not yet accessible for all and is not frontier). If this trend continues my base case is that only Anthropic will represent the U.S. as a true frontier model maker.
Routers and harnesses took on increasing importance as a majority of tokens are now generated from agent swarms and not people.
BigTech Capex means the U.S. is betting on compute to stay ahead of China, which keeps Europe far behind. It’s estimated Capex could reach around $1.3 Tr in 2027. Europe for its part doesn’t have the capital to keep up. While France’s Mistral is well funded, it hasn’t been able to keep up with Chinese open-weight model makers.
In 2026, the label "AI Bank" (or the "Central Bank of AI") emerged to describe Nvidia’s transition from a pure hardware vendor into the chief financial orchestrator powering the artificial intelligence ecosystem. Nvidia began heavily leveraging financial engineering, structured debt, and asset-backed lending to ensure that capital keeps flowing into data center construction and GPU procurement thereby putting its soon to be $6 Trillion valuation into question. Nvidia has since done $122.9 billion in buybacks lone since 2023 to Q1 of 2026.
The full State of AI 2026 Report is 244 slides, why not skim it yourself.
Nathan and his team are somehow giving Karratha credit for this. 🚨RSI led to a pipeline of supposed AI startups working on this in a professional and serious capacity including many and multiple former Google DeepMind teams. Outside of the capital going to Humanoids (Physical AI) it’s the biggest capital wastage we’ve seen yet in the AI boom (late 2023 to the present).
This included a significant rise in RSI related AI paper.
There are still dozens to hundreds to thousands of cybersecurity incidents where Astra’s model are responsible by OpenAI. Lawsuits have already started against OpenAI.
Firms making the heaviest investments in generative AI saw their total employment grow by roughly 10% over the two years following adoption.
Companies with low AI spending experienced no statistically significant change in overall employment compared to non-adopting control groups.
AI is getting cheaper and faster than any prior transformative technology. (chart from EpochAI). Read More.
What’s next? A cure for all varieties of Cancer?
Reports indicate that BigTech appear to be slowing Anthropic usage five weeks before their IPO simultaneously. This is partly due to Meta and Microsoft urging employees to use their own models and AI tools.
Read more around this trend (Sept, 2026).
While humanoid robotics startups saw a huge splurge of Venture Capital deals. Embodied AI, physical AI and the humanoid form factor appear to dominate in a race to robot supremacy. A race where in some aspects, China may actually be ahead.
Top embodied AI startups are marking some rather incredible claims. It’s Skild AI and Generalist AI that are the two startups in question, not Sunday Robotics. (Nathan’s VC inserts his own companies that he has funded into these slides).
AI companies are turning to human labor for video data generation. Often not compensating these workers who are usually in poorer countries adequately.
An internal general-purpose reasoning model at OpenAI disproved Erdős's Planar Unit Distance Conjecture (originally posed in 1946).
Following the announcement, discussions surfaced across technical communities questioning whether model training included proprietary mathematical research or private prompt logs from previous user chats (such as Codex sessions where mathematicians brainstormed related problem structures).
So this is up to slide 82 where we get to the section on Industry that we will continue in a future post.
You can listen or watch to Nathan’s introduction directly. The video is 15 minutes long.
2026 has so far had a lot of interesting themes. It’s not clear how the Anthropic IPO will perform in the macro and bond yield stress we are seeing in capital markets as of October.
SpaceX while having limited AI capabilities in either models, products, momentum or orbital compute, somehow has managed to rebound from a post IPO dip in the summer. The climate for Anthropic and OpenAI could be considerably different to worse.
